body.objective: Join the validated horizon-to-infinity connection with the exact null-infinity Lee-Wald trace forms and classify the globally populated finite-flux axial Schwarzschild channels.
body.stop_condition: For ell=2, M=1 and positive-frequency profiles supported in omega in (1/2,3/4), import the validated 6x3 connection T(omega), its exact ordered infinity coordinates and current-conservation enclosure, together with the exact I-minus/I-plus wave-packet trace maps and endpoint Gram forms G_minus(omega), G_plus(omega). Require an explicit exact crosswalk from the raw horizon-initializer complex order [XH0a,XH0b,EH0,XHplus,EHout,XHminus] to the public order [XH0a,XH0b,XHplus,XHminus,EH0,EHout], and verify that the propagated future-regular raw columns are [0,1,2]. Pull the endpoint forms back to the future-horizon-regular coefficient bundle without choosing sampled eigenvectors. On a finite rational subdivision, determine by exact or validated interval algebra: the dimensions of the globally populated matching-trace spaces; the kernel intersections and quotient dimensions; the ranks, radicals and inertias of the pulled-back flux forms; whether any additional Bach direction survives horizon regularity, complete metric reconstruction and finite endpoint flux; and every exceptional frequency cell where the classification is unresolved or changes. Prove the orientation-correct conservation relation between the horizon and endpoint forms on the populated quotient. Extend the multiplier classification to compactly supported wave packets by the already certified differentiated bounds. If the data suffice, construct the induced incoming-to-outgoing relation and prove its J-isometry; otherwise state the exact missing boundary block rather than calling the partial relation a scattering matrix. Include an independent verifier and mutations that delete an additional coordinate, apply public selector [0,1,4] directly to the raw initializer, swap I-minus/I-plus orientation, identify the radial and endpoint currents, flatten across an exceptional wall, or infer a positive metric from inertia alone.
body.current_gate: Global finite-flux channel and flux-signature classification
body.forbid: no formal infinity vector called a global mode; no horizon-regular column called finite flux before applying the exact trace quotient; no sampled singular value called rank; no unresolved cell crossed by continuity; no monochromatic generalized mode called finite energy; no radial Wronskian called null flux; no partial boundary relation called a full scattering matrix; no CPT, pole-freeness, stability, positivity or unitarity claim without a separate theorem
body.resource_hint: Preserve the infinity order XI0,XI1,XI2,XI3,EI0,EI2 and the exp(+i omega v) convention. The public horizon selector [0,1,4] belongs to the public label order and must never be applied to the raw initializer; in the raw order the future-regular selector is [0,1,2]. Work with quotient maps and Gram pullbacks, not basis-dependent signs. A result that the globally populated extra quotient is empty, nonzero positive, nonzero indefinite, radical, or exceptional is equally terminal when proved on the declared cells.
notes: This is the Phase-3 join: it turns separate formal trace and global radial results into the first physical-channel verdict.
A full two-boundary scattering operator is optional and must not be inferred unless the imported connection data span the required incoming boundary bundle.
